ARCL 103.course_name: Introduction to Archaeology: Past Perspectives and Future Promise
ARCL 103.description: A critical introductory overview to the discipline of archaeology, its functions and entanglements, and potential contributions and transformations for the future.

ARCL 140.description: The origin and evolution of the human lineage and the emergence of human biological and cultural traits with emphasis on the fossil record before the Pleistocene.

ARCL 203.description: Introduces the methods and principles applied in anthropological archaeology and cultural-historical research.

ARCL 204.description: An examination of some momentous discoveries in archaeology that have shaped our knowledge of the ancient world and the history of humanity.

ARCL 228.description: The application of methods from biological anthropology and archaeology to the identification, recovery, and analysis of skeletal remains from crime scenes, mass disasters, and unexplained deaths.

ARCL 231.description: Introductory survey of North American archaeology comparing the ancient cultures from all major regions of Canada and the US.

ARCL 232.description: The archaeology of ancient Mexico, Central and South America, highlighting recent discoveries about the emergence and growth of civilizations such as the Aztecs, Maya, Zapotec, Inca, Chimor and their ancestors.

ARCL 235.course_name: Taming the Wild: Animals, Alcohol and Agriculture
ARCL 235.description: How, when and why humans became dependent on cultivated foods and domestic animals and the methods used to document plant and animal domestication.

ARCL 305.description: Current theoretical developments explored through the practice of archaeology. Examples drawn from a range of times and places focusing on emerging technologies, food production, colonial encounters and culture contact, materiality and symbolic systems, social inequality and complexity, and human-environmental interactions.

ARCL 306.description: Intensive training in excavation techniques and interpretation, including mapping procedures, recording, preliminary analysis, and reporting. Students will participate in an excavation for the Summer Session and will use this excavation as a basis for lectures, discussions and reports. Additional Field Trip Fees are charged for this course.

ARCL 309.course_name: The Archaeology of Collapse and Sustainability
ARCL 309.description: An evaluation of the issues of sustainability and collapse of ecological and social systems through the archaeological study of the past.

ARCL 318.description: Early hunter-gatherer-forager societies, spanning the period from the emergence of the first tool-using hominins to the origins of agriculture.

ARCL 319.course_name: The Emergence of Complex Societies in Eurasia and Africa
ARCL 319.description: Archaeological evidence and theories for the origins and spread of settled village life, food production systems, and complex social and political organization: Early Neolithic period through to the appearance of the old world civilizations.

ARCL 322.course_name: Archaeological Foundations of East and Southeast Asia
ARCL 322.description: Survey of the archaeology of East and Southeast Asia, with an emphasis on the beginnings of the economic, social, political, and artistic traditions and systems of the great civilizations, and the conditions in which they arose. Theories of cultural development emphasizing Neolithic and state-level societies will be discussed.

ARCL 323.description: The archaeology of Mexico and Central America with an emphasis on the emergence of economic, social, political, and religious organization. Seminar format discussing recent research and current discoveries.

ARCL 324.description: The archaeology of South America with an emphasis on the emergence of economic, social, political, and religious organization, and a primary focus on the Andean region. Seminar format with lectures discussing recent research and current discoveries.

ARCL 325.description: Origin and development of the hominins; the hominin fossil record, and theories relating to hominin evolution. Prerequisite: ARCL 140.

ARCL 326.description: A comprehensive survey of primates, with emphasis on evolution, ecology, social organization, social behaviour, and field studies. Prerequisite: ARCL 140.

ARCL 345.description: Molecular techniques in archaeology and their application to anthropological and archaeological research.

ARCL 405.description: Current methods in mapping spatial information in archaeology and related subfields of anthropology.

ARCL 406.description: A survey of methods and techniques in the interpretation of archaeological data; practical experience in processing and analyzing archaeological materials by means of a research project. Students will prepare manuscripts, drawings and photographs for publication and will learn the basics of lithic and faunal analyses.

ARCL 410.description: Analysis of the archaeology of a specific areal, methodological, and theoretical topic, including a summary of the literature and examination of specific sites and analytical issues. The area covered will vary according to the instructor's expertise.

ARCL 411.course_name: Prehistory of a Special Area in the New World
ARCL 411.description: Analysis of the prehistory of a selected New World area, including a summary of the literature and discussion of relevant problems. The course will provide background for students in North, Central, and South American area studies. Typical offerings include the prehistory of Mesoamerica, the Southwest, North America and the Mayan areas.

ARCL 419.description: A survey of methods, theory, and case-studies in mortuary archaeology. Prerequisite: ARCL 203.

ARCL 420.course_name: First Nations Archaeology of British Columbia
ARCL 420.description: An advanced study of the prehistoric archaeology of coastal and interior Native Peoples. A critical analysis of the archaeological evidence and interpretations of prehistoric cultural developments from the earliest migrations up to historical contact.

ARCL 424.course_name: Practising Archaeology and the Management of Cultural Resources
ARCL 424.description: Survey of the use of archaeology in the public context and interest, particularly the identification, evaluation, conservation, and management of archaeological resources. Laws and policies, principles, methods, and ethical concerns guiding current practices, public involvement, relationships with indigenous communities, and contemporary issues in cultural resources management.

ARCL 425.description: The archaeological evidence for the change of human diets over time and the methods used to reconstruct past diets.

ARCL 430.description: Analytical and practical skills in locating archaeological sites and data leading to spatial patterns and historical interpretation.

ARCL 435.course_name: Culture Through the Animal Body: Fundamentals of Zooarchaeology
ARCL 435.description: Methods to study animal bones and shell remains to understand the ways that people acquired food, negotiated their social status, and contributed to ceremonial practices. Prerequisite: ARCL 103.
